evidence: In all three 3D views every visible body (ESP32 module, both tact switches, USB-C, pin header, passives) is spatially distinct with no intersecting or stacked bodies.
In 3d_iso and 3d_iso_back all bodies sit flush on the PCB surface with no floating, sunken, or tilted parts; the USB-C overhang at the edge is normal for that connector.

In 3d_top each visible body is centered over its own pad pattern (module over its castellated pads, switches over their 4-pad clusters, USB-C over its pad row), with no body displaced from its footprint.
USB-C J1 opens outward toward the bottom-right board edge and header J2 sits along the left edge; there are no relays, and the single polarized part shows no inconsistent orientation.
The dashed antenna keepout sits along the top board edge directly above the ESP32 antenna section and contains no components, pads, or visible copper in the 2D and 3d_top views.

C2 is stranded alone mid-board far from U1, R3/R4 float between the switch cluster and nothing, J2 is isolated in the bottom-left corner, and large empty regions on the right and center make the layout read as scattered rather than tight grid-aligned clusters.
